mont_elder.text: I grew up in Plymouth. The street I lived on is under six metres of ash. Sometimes I think I can still hear the clock.
We came to Little Bay. We built again. We're good at it. We've had practice.

mont_birder_n.text: The Montserrat oriole: black and bright yellow, the national bird, found nowhere else. It nests high in the banana and heliconia leaves of the Centre Hills.
After the eruption most of its forest was gone, and the population crashed. We protect what's left. We're slowly winning.

mont_cook.text: Goat water: goat meat, cloves, thyme, hot pepper, breadfruit if I'm feeling generous. National dish, so be polite.
It's called water because it's a broth. It's called goat because it's goat. We keep things simple.

then.text: The grey bank is full of tiny pale glassy specks. You've already got a sample jar.

else.text: You kneel at the boundary and scoop a handful of ash into the sample jar. It's fine as flour and very slightly warm. It sparkles in the sun.
A drift of fine grey ash, soft as flour. It's from the volcano. It's still falling, in tiny amounts, from time to time.

mont_guide.text: Welcome to Montserrat. We say 'Emerald Isle'. We mean it. The north is green and the south is grey. Please stay in the north.
St Patrick's Day is our big week: masquerade, music, food and the holiday. Don't ask me which saint is the patron of volcanoes. We've checked.

mont_home.text: The flight to Brize Norton goes via Antigua for the sake of the schedule, but you'll not notice. The RAF has other ideas.
Head home to RAF Brize Norton?

then.text: Right-o. Keep an eye on the plume as we take off.

else.text: Take your time. We'll be here.

montserrat_bureau.text: Welcome to the bureau de change. Local money in, sterling out, or the other way round. A small fee, and a very small queue.

montserrat_homebound.text: Heading back to the mainland? Passage to RAF Brize Norton can be arranged whenever you like. Bring your own sandwiches.
